questions.q: Who is not allowed to enter the assembly of Yahweh?
questions.a: A man whose male organ is crushed or cut off, or a child from intermarriage and that person’s descendants to the tenth generation, are not allowed to enter the assembly of Yahweh.

questions.q: Why are Ammonites and Moabites not allowed to enter the assembly of Yahweh?
questions.a: They are not allowed to enter because they did not provide the Israelites with food and water when the Israelites came out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam to curse the Israelites.

questions.q: What evidence showed that Yahweh did not listen to Balaam?
questions.a: Yahweh turned Balaam’s curse into a blessing for Israel.

questions.q: Why should they not detest the Edomites and Egyptians?
questions.a: They are not to detest the Edomites because they are considered relatives of the Israelites as they are descendants of Isaac. The Egyptians should not be detested because the Israelites once lived as foreigners in Egypt.

questions.q: If a man in the Israelite army becomes unclean because of what happens during the night, what must he do to become clean and return to the camp?
questions.a: He must go outside the camp until evening. Then he must bathe in water, and at sunset he can return to the camp.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh give instructions to the people of Israel about where and how to relieve themselves?
questions.a: Yahweh was walking in the midst of their camp, so the camp must be holy in order that Yahweh would not see any unclean thing and turn away from them.

questions.q: What are the instructions concerning a slave who escapes from their master?
questions.a: Such a slave is not to be returned to their master. They are to be allowed to live among the Israelites in any town they choose, and they must not be mistreated.

questions.q: Why were male and female cultic prostitutes not allowed among the Israelites, and why were their earnings not allowed to be brought as a vow into Yahweh’s house?
questions.a: These practices and the earnings from them are considered an abomination to Yahweh.

questions.q: How is the policy for charging interest different for fellow Israelites compared to foreigners?
questions.a: Israelites are not to charge interest to other Israelites on loans of money, food, or anything else. However, they are allowed to charge interest to foreigners.

questions.q: How important is it for an Israelite to fulfill a vow made to Yahweh?
questions.a: It is very important. An Israelite must not delay in fulfilling a vow made to Yahweh because Yahweh requires it, and failing to do so is a sin. They must do what they have voluntarily promised.

questions.q: What are Israelites allowed to do when passing through a neighbor’s vineyard or grain field?
questions.a: When in a neighbor’s vineyard, they are allowed to eat as many grapes as they want but not to put any in a container to take with them. When in a neighbor’s grain field, they are allowed to pluck ears of grain by hand but not to use a sickle to cut the stalks.

commentary.text: Who are shut out from the congregation.
Of fugitive servants, Usury, and other precepts.

Verses 1–8 We ought to value the privileges of God's people, both for ourselves and for our children, above all other advantages. No personal blemishes, no crimes of our forefathers, no difference of nation, shuts us out under the Christian dispensation. But an unsound heart will deprive us of blessings; and a bad example, or an unsuitable marriage, may shut our children from them.
The camp of the Lord must have nothing offensive in it. If there must be this care taken to preserve the body clean, much more should we be careful to keep the mind pure.

It is honourable to shelter and protect the weak, provided they are not wicked. Proselytes and converts to the truth, should be treated with particular tenderness, that they may have no temptation to return to the world. We cannot honour God with our substance, unless it be honestly and honourably come by. It must not only be considered what we give, but how we got it. Where the borrower gets, or hopes to get, it is just that the lender should share the gain; but to him that borrows for necessary food, pity must be showed. That which is gone out of thy lips, as a solemn and deliberate vow, must not be recalled, but thou shalt keep and perform it punctually and fully. They were allowed to pluck and eat of the corn or grapes that grew by the road side; only they must not carry any away. This law intimated what great plenty of corn and wine they should have in Canaan. It provided for the support of poor travellers, and teaches us to be kind to such, teaches us to be ready to distribute, and not to think every thing lost that is given away. Yet it forbids us to abuse the kindness of friends, or to take advantage of what is allowed. Faithfulness to their engagements should mark the people of God; and they should never encroach upon others.
